why: the count-based acceptance rule was measured against identical text and fired twice in three pairs

method.identical_text_pairs: arms whose payload files are byte-identical, re-run in a different epoch; three exist on disk
method.drift_unit: one (task, dimension) cell per pair; a cell counts as better/worse when the pass fraction moves
method.z: two-proportion z over pooled run marks, dimension gated only when >= 4 tasks score it

between_epoch_drift.caveat: cells from the same transcripts are not independent and the three pairs span only two epoch transitions (e7->e8 supplies two); read this as 'drift exists and is downward', not as a calibrated p

false_alarm_on_identical_text.z_rule_after_probe_repair: still 0 of 3; worst identical-text z is -1.69

known_limits_of_the_new_rule.power: a ~20% relative degradation is invisible to BOTH rules at this budget; z buys false-alarm control and n-invariance, not sensitivity
known_limits_of_the_new_rule.multiplicity: e5-cch-borrows fullrc put four dimensions down at once (worst z -1.94) and would PASS a max-z rule; that epoch's rejection was later overturned on sonnet (e6) and shipped as v0.6.2, but the hole is real — hence the secondary clause
known_limits_of_the_new_rule.saturation: gate_ran now sits at 16/16 on base in e8/e9/e10: the suite can see a >=4-run collapse there, never an improvement
known_limits_of_the_new_rule.multiplicity_retracted: the e5-cch-borrows example above is withdrawn: two of those four dimensions were measured by probes repaired later the same day. Re-scored, that comparison PASSES the whole rule (worst z -1.51), so the two-dimension clause has no supporting example on disk.
